questions.stem: Basisphenoid fuses with basioccipital at what age?
questions.solutionHtml:
18—25 years
  • The basilar part of the occipital bone (also basioccipital) extends forward and upward from the foramen magnum, and presents in front an area more or less quadrilateral in outline.
  • In the young skull this area is rough and uneven, and is joined to the body of the sphenoid by a plate of cartilage.
  • By the twenty-fifth year this cartilaginous plate is ossified, and the occipital and sphenoid form a continuous bone.


KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd edition, Page number- 79,80.

questions.stem: Blue colored gastric mucosa on autopsy is due to poisoning by:
questions.solutionHtml:
Copper

Blue discoloration of gastric mucosa is commonly seen with poisonings with copper sulfate, copper succinate, dyes such as methylene blue, toluidine blue and food coloring agents.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd edition, Page number- 547.

questions.stem: In Maastricht classification of donation after cardiac death which category is stage 3?
questions.solutionHtml:
Awaiting cardiac arrest
  • In Maastricht, the classification of organ donation after cardiac death of a patient awaiting cardiac arrest is category III.
  • Category III donors are patients on intensive care units with non-survivable injuries who have treatment withdrawn; where such patients wished in life to be organ donors, the transplant team can attend at the time of treatment withdrawal and retrieve organs after cardiac arrest has occurred.
